text:
maya: running the weekly DAST against staging — it's failing auth for the login flow, returns 302 -> /sso/login every time. started ~10:05am.
alex: can you paste the failing request/response? what sequence of redirects?
maya: here's the curl repro (sanitized):
```
curl -v -L -I 'https://staging-app.example.com/' -H 'User-Agent: DASTScanner/1.0' -x 10.0.0.2:8080
```
maya: response shows a redirect chain and missing X-Forwarded-User header when proxied via staging-auth-proxy. scanner ends up at generic login page.
sam: we rolled an RBAC tweak in frontdoor earlier this morning — removed the impersonation passthrough for service accounts (CR: fd-2026). could be related.
alex: if frontdoor dropped the header, the auth-proxy won't detect scanner as service account. maya, can you verify header is present when hitting the origin directly (bypass proxy)?
maya: hitting origin directly returns 200 and has `X-Forwarded-User: scanner@redwood-ci` in the response log. when routed through frontdoor+auth-proxy header is absent.
lia: security-bot flagged an audit log gap around 09:58 for KMS-rotation job — might be unrelated but worth noting: rotation job triggered log pruning.
security-bot: ALERT: KMS audit-write suppressed during `kms-rotate-2026-03`. See run 2026-03-18T09:58Z.
sam: oh crap. the RBAC tweak plus a KMS log suppression could make triage harder if we need to prove scanner access. but immediate fix is to re-enable the passthrough for the scanner service account or add a specific allowlist for DAST traffic.
alex: agree. mitigation options: 1) revert fd-2026 for the scanner service account only (fast); 2) update auth-proxy to inject a verified header for known scanner CIDRs (medium); 3) run DAST with an ephemeral bearer token that bypasses SSO flow (requires scanner config). Which do we want?
maya: option 1 gets scans green in ~5min. option 3 is good for CI hygiene (avoid depending on header passthrough) but needs token router change.
lia: while we fix, we should capture evidence for any findings — with KMS audit suppression we might need extra proof. action: run a targeted DAST with origin-bypass and save full request/response dumps.
alex: assigned: sam to revert allowlist for scanner, maya to run origin-bypass DAST and collect artifacts, lia to coordinate audit evidence collection and escalate KMS audit gap to infra. target: 30min.
sam: starting revert now. ping me if deploy blocks. :hammer_and_wrench:
maya: running an origin-bypass DAST now with `--save-traffic` option. will upload dump to /tmp/dast-staging-1749900000.tar.gz and link it here.
security-bot: Deploy notice: fd-config frontdoor updated by sam at 10:12Z (change fd-2026-revert-scanner). No downtime expected.
sam: revert applied. can someone re-run scanner?
maya: re-run queued — immediate improvement, now getting 200s through proxy. initial spikes of 429 on some endpoints (rate-limit).
alex: add temporary scan CIDR to rate limit whitelist for 30m while we catch up. I've opened a short-lived rule `rl-allow-dast-30m`.
lia: audit checklist: save DAST tarball, export frontdoor access logs for the 09:50-10:20 window, collect KMS rotation run logs and the rotation CI job artifact. I'll create an incident tracker and attach artifacts.
maya: uploaded dump: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/dast/1749900000-dump.tar.gz (only team access).
sam: heading to update PR notes for fd-2026 revert and will follow up with a safer policy design (no broad passthroughs; scanner gets a short-lived token flow).
alex: long-term: we should update DAST to use token-based auth and add unit tests to catch header-drop regressions (test harness that sits behind frontdoor). also add an alert if scanner health-checks start failing for >2 runs.
ia: +1 for automated smoke-check after frontdoor changes. low-friction test prevents this.
lia: closing loop: incident doc -> /incidents/2026-03-18-dast-auth-proxy.json. owners: sam (remediate policy), maya (scan artifacts), lia (audit evidence). leaving channel thread open for any follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
